items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I went to the prisons on Sunday with him after church to talk to prisoners... I had Reverend Johnson my minister over at the church... So we were good friends.

ctx.x: Yeah. Reverend Johnson would always tell about, don‟t be sitting down there in your finished basements thinking that everything is cool. There‟s a lot of people out there not happy so you‟ve got to get out there and do something about it instead of sitting in your finished basement. He would say about smoking, he said, “Fool at one end and fire at the other” [laughter]. So he was kind of a man that really got things going. I went to the prisons on Sunday with him after church to talk to prisoners. They were over…
It‟s absolutely good for you for sure. That‟s wonderful, thank you.
